title: Faith and Truth - Episode 2: The Word That Lights the Way

parts.style: warm, gentle late-night welcome, a soft smile in the voice, speaking slowly
parts.text: Welcome to SleepFit podcast series! This is Faith and Truth Episode 2! <chuckle> You may have already known me from episode one. I'm Sarah Mitchell. <short pause> Tonight, we're asking a question that often comes up when life feels uncertain... <short pause> how can I trust God's word, when I can't see what's ahead? <long pause>
We're looking at walking by faith... <short pause> and tonight, our focus is the word that lights the way. <short pause> But first, let's begin with a prayer. <long pause>
Father, quiet our hearts now. <short pause> Open our minds to your truth. <short pause> Help us hear what you want us to know tonight. <short pause> In Jesus' name... amen. <long pause>
There's an image in Scripture that has comforted believers for thousands of years. <short pause> You'll find it in Psalm one hundred nineteen... a long song of love for God's word. <long pause>
Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path. <long pause>

parts.style: slow, reflective, letting the words sink in
parts.text: A lamp unto my feet... <short pause> and a light unto my path. <long pause>

Think about that image for a moment. <short pause> In the ancient world, a lamp was a small clay vessel, filled with oil, with a wick that gave off a soft flame. <short pause> It didn't light up the whole road. <short pause> It didn't show you everything that lay ahead. <short pause> It showed you... the next step. <long pause>
And that's exactly what the psalmist is telling us about God's word. <long pause>

parts.style: gentle, a soft smile in the voice, illustrating
parts.text: We often want Scripture to be a floodlight, don't we? <chuckle> We want to open the Bible and find a detailed map of the next year... the next month... even the next week. <short pause> We want certainty. <short pause> We want to see the whole road, from here to there. <long pause>
But that isn't what God promises. <short pause> He promises a lamp for the next step... a light for the path right in front of you. <long pause>
And this matters, because faith isn't about knowing everything in advance. <short pause> Faith is trusting God... one step at a time. <long pause>
Now, you might be wondering... how does Scripture actually do that? <short pause> How does it light the next step? <long pause>
The apostle Paul wrote to a young pastor named Timothy, and explained what God's word is for. <long pause>

All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness: That the man of God may be perfect, throughly furnished unto all good works. <long pause>

parts.style: slow, deliberate, each phrase landing softly
parts.text: All Scripture, Paul says, is given by inspiration of God. <short pause> And it's profitable. <short pause> That word means useful... beneficial... valuable. <short pause> Profitable for doctrine... <short pause> teaching us what is true. <short pause> For reproof... <short pause> showing us what is not. <short pause> For correction... <short pause> showing us how to get back on track when we've wandered. <short pause> And for instruction in righteousness... <short pause> teaching us how to live in a way that pleases God. <long pause>

Paul goes on... that the man of God may be perfect, thoroughly furnished unto all good works. <short pause> And perfect here means complete. Mature. Equipped for what God has called you to do. <long pause>

So here's what this means. <short pause> Scripture doesn't necessarily tell you which job to take, or which house to buy, or whether to send that email tomorrow. <short pause> But it does something better. <short pause> It shapes the person who makes those decisions. <long pause>

It teaches you who God is... faithful, holy, loving, just. <short pause> It teaches you who you are... made in his image, fallen, redeemed, loved. <short pause> It teaches you how God works... through grace, through patience, through ways that often surprise us. <short pause> And when you know those things... you have light for the next step. <long pause>

Let me give you an example. <short pause> Suppose you're facing a choice tomorrow, and you're not sure what to do. <short pause> You open Scripture, and you don't find a verse that says, Do this specific thing. <short pause> But you read about God's character... about his faithfulness to those who trust him. <short pause> You read about his wisdom, and how he guides his people. <short pause> You read a command to love your neighbor... or to speak the truth... or to do your work as unto the Lord. <long pause>
And suddenly... you have light. <short pause> You don't see the whole road. But you see the next faithful step. <long pause>

This is what it means for God's word to be a lamp. <short pause> It's not that Scripture answers every question we bring to it. <short pause> It's that Scripture equips us to walk faithfully... with the questions we carry. <long pause>

And here's the other side of this truth. <short pause> If we're only looking for a floodlight, we might miss the lamp that's already shining. <short pause> We might overlook what God is showing us right now... because we're anxious about what we can't see further down the road. <long pause>

But when we accept that God gives light for one step at a time... we're free to take that step. <short pause> Free to obey what we already know. <short pause> Free to trust that when we need the next piece of guidance... God will give it. <long pause>

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: So tonight, as you rest... consider this. <short pause> You don't need to see the whole road. <short pause> You don't need to have everything figured out before morning. <short pause> What you need is to know God... and to trust that his word is enough light for the step in front of you. <exhales> And it is. <long pause>

Let's close with a word of prayer. <long pause> Father, thank you for your word. <short pause> Thank you that it is a lamp, steady and true, showing us the way one step at a time. <short pause> Help us to trust you with what we cannot see... <short pause> and to walk faithfully in the light you've already given. <short pause> In Jesus' name... amen. <long pause>
Good night.
